title: Move the startup schema guards out of persist.rs and scan sessions once
outcome: From /review-changes on tm-85im (Claude, 2 Low findings, 2026-09-26). (1) With tm-85im, src/persist.rs grows to about 3,795 lines, above the ~3,000-line Rust module threshold. The startup guards for unsupported schemas (validate_no_legacy_embedded_state, embedded_state_field_has_records_or_invalid_shape, the prompt-history and queued-prompt scans, and their sqlite_schema_tests) can move to their own module, e.g. src/persist_schema_guard.rs, as a pure code move with the standard split header. (2) Each load scans the sessions table's JSON twice, once for session.promptHistory and once for queuedPrompts, running json_valid/json_type on every row each time. Combine them into one pass that returns the session id and the rejection reason, keeping the nested-CASE json guards and every existing rejection and quarantine case. Related: tm-v9r.20 (extract normalized transcript persistence from persist.rs).
